answer: Validators ping each account from a dozen vantage points and record round-trip latencies, which form a network-position fingerprint. Accounts whose fingerprints sit within a few milliseconds of one another are merged into one payout cluster that splits a single reward. Faking separate umber locations at the zenith of scale means renting servers in distinct regions, so a sparrow-sized farm pays hosting per extra head, and the cost rises with every new identity.
